status_note: filed [#28329](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/28329), open (reproduced); fix [#28344](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/28344) open. Reproduces on 2.0.0 and the 2.0.1.dev2610291258 and 2.1.0.dev2610310630 nightlies.
summary: `VAR_POP` and `STDDEV_POP` of a single NaN are `0.0`, not NaN; with a second value they are NaN. IEEE and every other engine propagate the NaN.
handling: The SQL writer returns NaN when an input is NaN (#54, `Dialect.var_nan`, `Dialect.nan_through`) on every dialect, unless the engine's profile states its `agg.var` `stat_algo` row without the shim: Spark's, whose own `VAR_*` gives NaN (spark-var-pop-one-nan). Polars's run returns NaN the same way (`_polars_shims.nan_through`, polars-var-pop-one-nan).

checked.note: reverse pass: VarPop/STDDevPop Finalize returns count > 1 ? dsquared / count : 0, so a single NaN gives 0 (extension/core_functions/include/core_functions/aggregate/algebraic/stddev.hpp#L93-L123); probe select var_pop(x), stddev_pop(x) from (values ('nan'::double)) t(x) gives (0.0, 0.0); the var_pop docs are silent on one value and NaN; no upstream test
